Confirmed on `v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]` and `v4.5.beta.custom_build [71a994815]`. I don't know that I would have necessarily expected collisions to work properly in a canvas layer, but it is certainly strange that only one of the intersect methods does not work.

```
Godot v4.5.beta (71a994815) - macOS Sequoia (15.5.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 (Apple7) - Apple M1 (8 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory
```

This behavior is expected.
The [PhysicsPointQueryParameters2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_physicspointqueryparameters2d.html#class-physicspointqueryparameters2d-property-canvas-instance-id) has an attribute `canvas_instance_id`. At default it uses the main viewport canvas. For custom CanvasLayers it has to be set.
I used the following code in the `cast_point` function of the MRP and now get a result for both cases.
```gdscript
if canvas_item.get_canvas_layer_node() != null:
	point_query.canvas_instance_id = canvas_item.get_canvas_layer_node().get_instance_id()
```

I am not sure why this parameter only exists for the point query, but that's the reason it is the only case that fails.
I am also not sure how to resolve this. Just leave it as is, because it is technically a user error, adjust the documentation (where?) or even add the `canvas_instance_id` to the other `*_intersect()` methods, even though that would definitely break some existing user code?

Thanks for clarifying what `canvas_instance_id` does! Talking to other users it seems like a workaround for this as of now is to just use raycasts with size 0 - apparently they get clamped to a non-zero value internally so they end up acting just like a **PointCast** without having to deal with `canvas_instance_id`.

> I am not sure why this parameter only exists for the point query, but that's the reason it is the only case that fails. I am also not sure how to resolve this. Just leave it as is, because it is technically a user error, adjust the documentation (where?) or even add the `canvas_instance_id` to the other `*_intersect()` methods, even though that would definitely break some existing user code?

Actually, I kept asking myself the same thing but... doesn't it make more sense that instead of breaking these extremely commonly used functions we decouple the logic of **PointCasts** relying on anything related to rendering? In my mind it doesn't make much sense to have rendering cause a physics bug, since it'd only display whatever physics has already calculated. A **CanvasLayer** interfering with the **PhysicsServer** in one very specific function just seems odd to me.

I fully agree.
So the solution is, to deprecate the `cavas_instance_id` parameter and remove it's logic?

> I fully agree. So the solution is, to deprecate the `cavas_instance_id` parameter and remove it's logic?

assuming that `intersect_point()` can work within multiple `CanvasLayers` i personally don't see a reason to keep `canvas_instance_id`. so yeah, deprecating it could be the simplest and cleanest solution.

Hey thread and devs who may stumble on this thread in future, I ran into this in my game (Godot 4.5.1) and wanted to share a quick workaround. My levels render inside a `SubViewport`, and `TileMapLayer` tiles have physics shapes on `physics_layer_0` with `collision_layer = 1`. `intersect_point()` silently returns empty results for **some** of these `TileMapLayer` physics bodies. Coordinates are correct, collision masks match, all transforms are identity. But I got really odd, inconsistent behavior. Tried `canvas_instance_id = 0` (default) and `canvas_instance_id = viewport.get_instance_id()`, neither helped. # Workaround Replaced `intersect_point()` with `intersect_shape()` using a tiny RectangleShape2D. ## Before (broken inside `SubViewport`) ``` var query := PhysicsPointQueryParameters2D.new() query.position = target_position query.collision_mask = collision_mask var result := space_state.intersect_point(query) ``` ## After (works correctly) ``` var query := PhysicsShapeQueryParameters2D.new() query.transform = Transform2D(0.0, target_position) query.collision_mask = collision_mask var shape := RectangleShape2D.new() shape.size = Vector2(2, 2) query.shape = shape var result := space_state.intersect_shape(query) ``` Cheers, Arran
